newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA SAYS PLANS CHINESE VENTURES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA SAYS PLANS CHINESE VENTURES.

text.p: Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s. said on Wednesday it hoped to sign several joint-venture contracts before the end of this year to produce trucks, cars, and engineering products in China.

Skoda, which makes products ranging from drink cans to nuclear machinery, said after a visit by China's Machinery Minister Bao Xuding that its exports to China should reach 300 million crowns this year, and rise 10 fold by the year 2000.
"The visit should help us to have several joint ventures established there (in China) before the end of this year," Skoda spokesman Karel Samec told Reuters.
Samec said the most advanced project in the pipeline was a joint venture with Shanghai Heavy Machinery to make forging products.

Other plans to be concluded by the year's end included making of Skoda unit Tatra trucks and Beta passenger cars in China from imported kits, which Samec said would gradually be replaced by China-made parts.
Samec declined to name Skoda's partners in the other China ventures.
Samec said the structures of the joint ventures were not yet defined, but added that the firm's "strategy is always to have a majority".
"All these projects are subject to approval either by local governments in the respective provinces, or by the central government in Beijing," Samec added.
Skoda a.s. is no longer affiliated with car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s., now a unit of Germany's Volkswagen AG. -- Jan Lopatka, Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2423-0003
